headline.title: Introducing Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber
headline.summary: New Gemini models have been launched, including Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber. These updates expand the Gemini lineup with enhanced features and capabilities.

articles.title: Data centers expected to use 4x more electricity by 2035
articles.summary: A report indicates that data centers constructed by 2033 are projected to consume four times more electricity than current levels, potentially matching India's total electricity usage. This significant increase raises concerns about energy sustainability and infrastructure demands in the coming years.

articles.title: Anthropic’s $1.5 billion book piracy settlement approved by judge
articles.summary: A federal judge has approved Anthropic's $1.5 billion settlement in a class action lawsuit with authors who alleged the company used copyrighted books to train its AI models. The settlement will provide approximately $3,000 to each author for their works involved in the case.

articles.title: Google releases three new Gemini models — but no 3.5 Pro
articles.summary: Google has launched three new Gemini models: 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and Flash Cyber. However, the absence of the anticipated Gemini 3.5 Pro has sparked discussions regarding the company's AI strategy.

articles.title: Jack Dorsey is taking on Slack with Buzz, a group chat platform for teams and their AI agents
articles.summary: Jack Dorsey has launched Buzz, a new group chat platform designed for workplace communication that integrates both human users and their AI agents. The platform aims to enhance team collaboration by facilitating conversations that include AI assistance.

articles.title: This Former Intel CEO Wants to Jumpstart Moore’s Law With Light
articles.summary: Former Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger is advocating for the use of light-based technology to advance Moore's Law, aiming to enhance the capabilities of artificial intelligence. His approach focuses on harnessing tiny beams of light to drive more powerful computing solutions.

articles.title: The State of Simulation for Physical AI: An Overview
articles.summary: The article provides an overview of the current advancements and challenges in simulation technologies for physical AI applications. It highlights the importance of realistic simulations in training AI systems for tasks involving physical interactions and the ongoing research aimed at improving these simulations.

articles.title: Introducing the ChatGPT for small business program
articles.summary: OpenAI has launched the ChatGPT for Small Businesses program, designed to assist entrepreneurs in developing AI skills and automating tasks using ChatGPT. The initiative aims to support small businesses in enhancing their operations and growth through AI technology.

articles.title: Music streamer Deezer says more than 50% of daily uploads are AI-generated
articles.summary: Deezer reported that over 50% of daily uploads to its platform are AI-generated, with more than 90,000 AI tracks uploaded each day in June. This trend highlights the growing influence of artificial intelligence in music production.

articles.title: A Sneaky Hacking Tool Targeting AI Infrastructure Is Lurking in Victims’ Blind Spots
articles.summary: A new malware targeting AI infrastructure has been discovered, capable of infiltrating coding systems to steal sensitive data and credentials. This tool can also activate a "death switch" to erase files and prevent legitimate users from accessing the system.

articles.title: Built for Vera Rubin, NVIDIA Spectrum-6 Arrives in Gigascale AI Factories
articles.summary: NVIDIA has introduced Spectrum-6, a networking solution designed for gigascale AI factories that utilize hundreds of thousands of GPUs and CPUs to train advanced AI models. This technology aims to enhance computing power and efficiency in generating intelligence at unprecedented scales.

articles.title: TreeSize won't renew perpetual-license support unless users subscribe
articles.summary: TreeSize has announced that it will no longer support perpetual licenses unless users subscribe to its new business model, citing "current economic conditions" as the reason for the change. This shift reflects a broader trend in software companies moving towards subscription-based services.
